` | Stable key for this turn's intent (required). Reuse it when retrying. |\n| `--session <sessionId>` | Continue this session ins
tead of starting one |\n| `--model <modelId>` | Provider-prefixed model id, e.g. `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`. Optional on the firs
t send: defaults to the selected environment’s or client’s model and is then pinned. A supplied ID must be provider-prefixed. |\n|
`--environment <environmentId>` | Target this environment's servers. Conflicts with `--server`. |\n| `--server <serverId...>` | T
arget these project servers. Conflicts with `--environment`. |\n| `--no-servers` | Start with no MCP servers. Conflicts with `--se
rver` and `--environment`; requires a backend with chat-environment support. |\n| `--system-prompt <text>` | System prompt for the
session |\n| `--tool-mode <mode>` | `read_only` (default) advertises only tools annotated `readOnlyHint: true`. `auto` advertises
everything and **may cause real side effects**. |\n| `--max-steps <n>` | Maximum engine steps this turn (1–16) |\n| `--max-tool-c
alls <n>` | Cap the tool calls this turn may make. `0` answers without tools. |\n| `--temperature <n>` | Sampling temperature (0–2
) |\n| `--effort <level>` | Reasoning effort for the model. First turn only: pinned to the session, refused with `--session`. It r
eplaces the temperature, so it cannot be combined with `--temperature`. Applied or refused by the rail the model runs on, never dr

opped |
| `--project <id-or-name>` | Project name or ID (required to start a session) |

`read_only` filters on a hint the SERV
ER asserts, so it is a policy this host applies rather than a guarantee it can verify. A server is free to annotate a mutating too

l as read-only.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Hosted session browsers require browser availability for your account and deployment. An unavai
lable browser reports a refusal or `browser.attached: false` with its reason. The live pane opens in the Playground when the brows
er workspace is enabled.\n\nAdd `--browser` to advertise browser tools for this turn. The first browser turn requires `--browser-m
ode allow_all|read_only|allowlist` unless the selected client supplies a browser policy. Optional `--browser-origins <origin...>`
and `--browser-tools <name...>` restrict that grant; `--browser-profile <profileId>` selects its initial saved profile. The grant
and profile are fixed thereafter. A client's current browser policy and the session's `read_only` tool mode may further restrict e
xecution.\n\nA continuation must opt in again with `--browser`; a plain send does not wake the desktop. Screenshots are returned a
s URLs and trace pointers. Use the printed **Open in Playground** link to view the transcript, take over the browser, and select *

*Resume agent** when finished. API session transcripts are view-only there.

### `cloud sessions browser`

Drive the session b
rowser without a model turn. All verbs except a new `open` require `--session <sessionId>`; use the public session ID, never its r

ead-only conversation UUID or logical browser ID.

| Verb | Description |
| - | - |
| `open` | Open or wake an existing sessio
n browser. Omit `--session` and provide `--project`, a browser policy, and a stable `--idempotency-key` to create an empty API ses
sion. |\n| `navigate <url>` | Navigate to an allowed URL. Use a stable `--command-id` for retries. |\n| `act --verb <verb>` | Act
on the page; pass `--target` as JSON and optional `--value` and `--expected-state`. |\n| `invoke <toolKey> --input <json>` | Invok
e a permitted page tool. |\n| `observe --mode <mode>` | Read the page; `--mode screenshot --download <dir>` saves screenshot evide

nce. |
| `note <text>` | Append a note to the command ledger. |
| `trace` | Read command receipts and screenshot URLs. |

# MCPJam API

> Programmatic access to the MCP servers in your MCPJam projects — diagnostics, tool calls, prompt rende

ring, and asynchronous eval runs.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **The MCPJam API is in preview.** It works today and we use it ourselves,
but\n> it has not been generally announced and the surface may change — including in\n> breaking ways — while we finish the design
. Pin your integration to the\n> behaviors documented on this page, build a [tolerant\n> reader](#versioning--stability), and expe
ct to revisit it. Feedback is very\n> welcome on [Discord](https://discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z) or\n> [GitHub](https://github.com/MCPJam

/inspector/issues).

> [card] [Create an API key](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys)
>
> Go straight to key management

in the hosted app. If you're signed out,
> you'll be asked to sign in and then land right back on the API keys page.

The MCPJa
m API lets you operate the MCP servers saved in your\n[hosted](https://docs.mcpjam.com/hosted/overview.md) projects — from CI, scr

ipts, or your own agents —
without opening the UI.

What you can do with it today:

* **Discover your resources** — list your

projects, their servers, eval
 suites, and chat sessions, so every ID the other routes need is
 self-serve
* **Validate a se
rver** — connect, initialize, and capture a capability snapshot\n* **Run the doctor** — the probe → connect → initialize → capabil
ities workflow\n* **Check OAuth requirements** — does this server need an OAuth grant?\n* **List tools, prompts, and resources** —
the server's MCP primitives\n* **Call a tool / render a prompt** — execute primitives and get the MCP result back verbatim\n* **R
ead a resource** by URI\n* **Export a full snapshot** — tools, resources, and prompts as one JSON document\n* **Manage a project's
clients** — list, read, **create** (from a built-in\n template like `claude`/`chatgpt`/`cursor`, or from a full config), edit,\n
duplicate, and delete the named, reusable configurations that define how\n MCPJam connects to and talks to your MCP servers. Ed
its are compare-and-set:\n read the client, then send its `configId` back as `expectedConfigId` for a\n config change and its `n
ame` back as `expectedName` for a rename — a rename\n does not rotate the config, so the config token cannot detect a concurrent\
n one — and a concurrent edit is rejected rather than silently reverted\n* **Manage a project's environments** — list, read, crea
te, edit, archive, and\n restore the named execution bundles (host + optional server group + optional\n pinned skills and plugin
versions) that eval suites and goals run against,\n and **preview** what one resolves to before launching it\n* **List a project
's studies** — name, access mode, attached servers, and\n share link — and **read one study's settings**: model, system prompt,\n
tool-approval policy, and resolved servers\n* **Author eval suites** — create a runnable suite (name, default model, servers, te
st cases) synchronously and get a `suiteId` back; no run is started and no credits are spent\n* **Run eval suites asynchronously**
— create a run from a saved suite, get a `202` + `runId`\n immediately, then poll status, per-iteration results (tool calls, tok

en
 usage, latency), and full traces. Runs appear live in the hosted UI,
 tagged `source: "api"`
* **Manage a server's acco
unts** — complete OAuth yourself (e.g. the SDK's\n `runOAuthLogin`, or your CI's own sign-in) and upload the token to a named\n
account; list, rename, choose the default, and delete accounts. Tokens are\n write-only: no route returns one\n* **Run a headless
agent turn** — send a message history, get back the\n assistant reply, the platform operations it invoked, references to any\n
resources it created (eval suites), and token usage; the model is pinned\n server-side and billed to the project\n* **Send feedba
ck** — report a bug, a missing capability, or something\n confusing to the MCPJam team at the moment you hit it; the same endpoin

t the
 `send_feedback` MCP tool calls

All endpoints operate on servers you have already added to a project in the
hosted ins

pector. Managing API keys remains UI-only — see
[Not in the API yet](#not-in-the-api-yet).
